body:
A gating gate row is a single sample: `_run_one` (`template/src/pdca_harness/gates.py:354`) runs the command once and the exit code is the verdict. When the substrate under the gate hiccups — a straggler from the previous leaf still holding a port, a momentary resource spike — that one sample records `fail`, `overall` flips red, and the bundle parks at AWAITING_SIGNOFF on a verdict that was never about the patch.

The harness already accepts that an oracle can fail to *answer*: a timed-out gate records `unverifiable`, not `fail`, precisely because "no verdict" must not be held against the fix (#46, #368). A `fail` contradicted by an immediately-following `pass` of the same command is the same epistemic situation reached one step later — the oracle gave no *reliable* verdict — but today it is indistinguishable from a reproducible red.

## Measured

getwyrd/wyrd-pdca `issue_648`, 2026-07-31, round 7: `C4-ci` (gating) recorded `cargo test --workspace --exclude wyrd-dst` exit 101 within ~90 seconds of a step that takes ~7 minutes green. All six prior rounds were green; the bundle-scoped `C4-verify` that ran seconds later was green; the reviewer's independent isolated run of the full gate was green; re-running the exact command in the exact worktree later that day was green. One transient sample cost the round its gating verdict, and the auto-iterate budget was already exhausted, so the red went straight into the human's §6.

## Suggested shape

On `fail` of a **gating** row whose command actually ran (not a `cmd_error` misconfiguration), run the same command once more, and record **both** verdicts:

- fail → fail: `fail`, evidence from the confirming run. The reproducible case is unchanged (one extra run of an already-red gate).
- fail → pass: `pass`, plus `flaky: true` and `attempts: ["fail", "pass"]` on the row, and a NEEDS-HUMAN item routed into SUMMARY §6 — classified HUMAN, not IMPL, so auto-iterate defers it instead of spending a rebuild round on it, while the C6 accept-guard still makes the human acknowledge the flake before an accept.
- fail → unverifiable/timeout: the first `fail` stands (the confirm run gave no verdict to overturn it with).

Bounds that keep it honest: exactly one confirm, gating rows only, never the model leaves (re-sampling a nondeterministic reviewer and discarding the disagreement is the opposite move — this re-samples a deterministic oracle and keeps both samples), and both attempts' output persisted via the gate log (#370). Cost is zero on green runs.

Config: `[gates] confirm_gating_fail = true`, default on, so an instance that wants raw single-sample verdicts can opt out.

A rendered instance (getwyrd/wyrd-pdca) is staging this locally, pending upstream.

comments.body: One refinement out of the instance staging's review pass: "never the model leaves" is not sufficient — a gate **row** can itself be model-backed (the instance's batched-review row runs 3 codex passes as a gate command), and the blanket confirm would re-sample that judge and let a second, luckier sample overwrite real first-run blockers as a flaky pass. The staged shape therefore adds a per-check opt-out — `confirm_fail = false` on the `[[gates.checks]]` entry, set on any model-backed row — alongside the project-wide `[gates] confirm_gating_fail` default.

title: gates: one transient red on a gating row parks the bundle — confirm a failed gating row once, recording both verdicts
